clue.text: Warden for president ?

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a warden as a presidential candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: Trollope's novel The Warden has Septimus Harding as its title character, and Warren G. Harding was the 29th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Septimus Harding is the title figure of Trollope's novel The Warden, while Warren Harding held the American presidency in the early 1920s.

clue.text: South African has steaming dram about ten

indicators.note: the whiskey measure sits about, around, the number

parts.note: steaming means hot
a dram or tot is a small measure of spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African drinks a steaming dram around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the drink around the number. The answer is a dated name for the Khoikhoi people, now regarded as offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The Khoikhoi people of southern Africa were formerly called by this name by European settlers.

clue.text: Practical chap alters one arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts letters into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth man rearranges something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' shuffles ALTERS with I.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a pragmatic person who accepts things as they are.

clue.text: Fretful announcement made to hospital receptionist ?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., what a sick person says on arrival

explanation.surface: A nervous new arrival speaks at the hospital desk.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretful means restless and irritable, and 'I'm a patient' is what someone tells the hospital desk.

clue.text: Dress. Gascons do it in reverse

indicators.note: the word is written in reverse, back to front

parts.note: people from Gascony were proverbially boastful, hence 'gasconade', so they brag

explanation.surface: A remark about dress: people of Gascony do it backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascons were famed braggarts in French stereotype, hence 'gasconade' for boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially a distinctive style of dress.

clue.text: Material for the males of various breeds

parts.note: a buck is the male of deer, rabbits and hares
a ram is the male sheep

explanation.surface: A breeder gathers fabric for the stud animals of several breeds.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two males of different species, joined side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and for stiffening clothes.

clue.text: Soldier arranged raid in aircraft

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes in the aircraft

parts.note: a bomber is a military aircraft

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A soldier organises a raid from an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' scrambles the raid, which the indicator 'in' then places inside the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the British artillery.

clue.text: Get a little lower ?

parts.note: read as begetting a small mooing creature, a young cow that lows

explanation.surface: Asking someone to drop down slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' looks like the comparative of low, but it is one that lows, a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow gives birth to her young, a little lowing animal.

clue.text: A tiger loose — eye-opener in Surrey

indicators.note: the letters are let loose into a new order
the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tiger escapes, a shock in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' shuffles A TIGER; the 'opener' of 'eye' is E. Reigate is a town in Surrey, a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a market town located in the county of Surrey, south of London.

clue.text: For disguises put request in writing

indicators.note: the request is put in the writing

parts.note: MS stands for manuscript, a piece of writing
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone asks in writing for disguises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... in' places the request inside the writing; 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Masks are face coverings worn as disguises.

clue.text: Super subject of a poet's autobiography

definitions.text: Super subject of a poet's autobiography

parts.words: Super subject of a poet's autobiography
parts.note: the Welsh poet W. H. Davies wrote The Autobiography of a Super-..., so the word that follows 'Super' in that title is wanted

explanation.surface: A poet writes a memoir about someone superb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super' looks like praise but is the first half of the hyphenated word in Davies's title.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Davies's 1908 memoir describes his life as a vagrant, a wandering homeless man.

clue.text: Recovers to hold motorway in battle

indicators.note: one word is told to hold another, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: a patient or market that recovers rallies
the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, here printed MI

explanation.surface: Someone regains strength to keep a motorway open during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, printed here with I for 1. 'to hold' places it inside the synonym for recovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramillies, in 1706, was one of Marlborough's great victories over the French in the War of the Spanish Succession.

clue.text: Arranges about many decrees

indicators.note: one word goes about, around, the other

parts.note: to arrange a text is to edit it
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: An official arranges a great number of decrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EDITS around C, the Roman hundred standing for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order issued by a ruler, i.e. a decree.

clue.text: French writer is after the beer-drinking room — wrong way

indicators.note: the little word comes after the rest, at the end
the phrase says these letters are to be read in the wrong direction, back to front

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a bar is a room for drinking

explanation.surface: A French author goes looking for the pub's taproom but heads the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong way' turns ALEBAR into RABELA; 'after' puts IS at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the sixteenth-century French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Main supporters of military bands

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and military bands are bodies of soldiers carried over it

explanation.surface: The chief backers of regimental music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like chief, but it is the sea; 'bands' are groups of soldiers, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships carrying soldiers across the sea bear up bodies of fighting men.

clue.text: In short, it helps with the tenth payment

annotationWithheld.why: In short, it helps with the tenth payment (5), answer TITHE: no parse of 'In short, it helps with the' gives the letters; the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: In short, it helps with the tenth payment

clue.text: Apple with meat rare ? That's about right

indicators.note: the phrase goes about, round, the single letter

parts.note: rare meat is red steak

explanation.surface: A diner asks for rare meat with an apple, and is told that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps RED STEAK round R; 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Redstreak is an old English cider apple variety with red-striped skin.

clue.text: Means to end ill-feeling

parts.note: read as a cure for feeling ill, a doctor's remedy, rather than reconciliation

explanation.surface: A way of ending resentment between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-feeling' suggests animosity, but read as feeling ill it calls for medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care is a means of curing sickness.

clue.text: Weekend with poor Lily, near Irish beauty-spot

parts.note: read as week-end, the final letter of the word week

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad, disordered state

explanation.surface: A weekend with Lily, who is poor, near an Irish beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weekend' looks like Saturday and Sunday but means the end of 'week'; 'poor' signals that the letters of Lily and near are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Killarney in County Kerry is famed for its lakes and scenery.

clue.text: Former majority figure

parts.note: the age at which a person used to come of age, reaching legal majority, before it was lowered to eighteen in 1969

explanation.surface: A one-time leading politician of the majority party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' suggests a winning party, but it is legal adulthood; 'figure' is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Until 1970 in Britain a person became a legal adult at twenty-one years old.

clue.text: Dominions seem troubled about rising rent

indicators.note: the troubled word goes about, around, the rising one
troubled letters are stirred into disorder
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a rip

explanation.surface: Dominions seem troubled about rents going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' scrambles seem into EMES; 'rising' turns the tear upwards in this down clue; 'about' wraps the scrambled letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Empires are realms ruled by one sovereign power.

clue.text: It held up Reynolds's work, no doubt

definitions.text: It held up Reynolds's work, no doubt

parts.words: It held up Reynolds's work, no doubt
parts.note: the painter Sir Joshua Reynolds would have rested his canvases on a stand while painting, rather than delaying anything

explanation.surface: Something delayed the painter Reynolds's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests a delay, but it means physically supported.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's wooden stand supports the canvas while the artist works.

clue.text: Rules upset vulgar summer visitor

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: rules are laws
vulgar means low, coarse

explanation.surface: Rules upset a coarse summer tourist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAWS into SWAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a migratory bird arriving in Britain for the summer.

clue.text: Value a little quiet commendation ?

parts.note: p, for piano, is the short musical marking for quiet
commendation is praise

explanation.surface: Someone values a small, quiet word of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the music direction piano, soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise something is to estimate its worth.

clue.text: Remains down under ?

definitions.meaning: a reference to Australia, where the ... cricket series is sometimes played

explanation.surface: Something left over in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket Test series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what remains after burning, and the cricket Ashes are contested between England and Australia, often in that country.

clue.text: Pole writing a poem

parts.note: a becomes an before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A Polish person composing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person but is an electrical terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode, one terminal of a battery or cell.

clue.text: A pastry item's put back in layers

indicators.note: the words are put back, read in reverse order of letters

parts.note: a tart is a pastry item; with the 's it becomes plural-looking TARTS

explanation.surface: A pastry is returned to its tin in layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses A TARTS, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or of society.

clue.text: Criminals go through Scotland

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for go, as in Burns's verse

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers travel across Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a band of criminals, and gang is the Scots verb meaning walk or depart.

clue.text: Used to play march in A-nothing new

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A band plays a march in A, with nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MARCH, IN, A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is an instrument someone uses for playing music.

clue.text: Letters written by Terry

parts.note: the letter L written out in full is ell
the letter N written out in full is en

explanation.surface: A collection of correspondence penned by someone called Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters spelt out as words; Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian actress whose letters were published.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Ellen Terry was the leading Shakespearean actress of the Victorian stage, so Terry is her surname.

clue.text: All these go on moon trip ?

definitions.text: All these go on moon trip

parts.words: All these go on moon trip
parts.note: before a lunar launch mission control declares 'all ... go', checking every component

explanation.surface: Everyone on a lunar voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All these go' reads as passengers but echoes the launch phrase 'All systems go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacecraft components and networks are checked and declared ready before launch.

clue.text: Escape.? Nonsense !

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, like 'come off it!'

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an escape story as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight from captivity, and 'get away!' is an exclamation of disbelief.
